correctness.rationale: The upper and lower bounds reconstruct to the same two-dimensional support-face quantity. For the upper bound, a center \(z_0=(cx,dy)\) and norm-one functional \((\alpha f,\beta g)\) produce slices whose coordinate norms approach the exposed face \(F_N(\alpha,\beta)\), giving the stated face maximum. For the lower bound, an arbitrary slice supplies \(p=(\|x_0\|,\|y_0\|)\) and \(h=(\|f\|,\|g\|)\); choosing a maximizing face point \(q=(a,b)\), the Daugavet slice characterization independently in each nonzero coordinate gives vectors almost antipodal to the normalized center while satisfying the coordinate functionals. A norming-functional argument yields coordinate distances at least \((1-\eta)(c+a)\) and \((1-\eta)(d+b)\). Absolute-norm monotonicity then gives the lower face value, including the zero-coordinate and zero-dual-coordinate boundary cases. Compactness of the positive unit sphere and exposed face justifies attainment and passage to the infimum.
risks: The theorem assumes nonzero real Daugavet spaces and an absolute normalized norm; it does not identify analogous formulas without the Daugavet property.

originality.rationale: The 2021 primary paper gives general direct-sum lower/upper estimates and exact \(\ell_p\) values, not the submitted arbitrary-absolute-norm exposed-face identity. Its Proposition 2.4 upper bound additionally uses an axis-extreme hypothesis, while the submitted formula covers every absolute normalized norm by optimizing all positive supporting faces. The 2026 Haller--Ostrak preprint is very close in topic and its abstract uses a suitable absolute norm on Daugavet summands to build an \(\ell_1\)-sum counterexample, but the full preprint could not be inspected in this run; that remains an explicit residual risk rather than grounds for rejection. Fresh Resultary search self-matched the audited record and returned distinct pointwise Daugavet-constant records, not a prior theorem implying the face formula.
residual_risks: The inaccessible full arXiv:2607.02227 preprint is a genuine close-source risk because its construction uses absolute sums of Daugavet spaces.

value.rationale: The theorem converts an infinite-dimensional sliced-thickness problem for all absolute sums of Daugavet spaces into one explicit two-dimensional face optimization. It strictly organizes the previously exact \(\ell_p\) cases and general bounds and supplies a reusable geometric reduction rather than an isolated numerical value.
risks: Computing the resulting scalar can still require a separate finite-dimensional optimization for a complicated absolute norm.
